A thread on
Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV)
Family: Paramyxoviridae
Genus: Metapneumovirus

Discovery
First Identified: In 2001 in the Netherlands, although it is believed to have been circulating for centuries. https://t.co/QDxf4Ik7Dg

nodes.author: vikramwagh
nodes.text:
Currently there are no vaccines approved for HMPV. 
Compared to Covid 19 its not a public health emergency

nodes.author: vikramwagh
nodes.text:
Treatment

Supportive Care: 

There is no specific antiviral treatment; management focuses on alleviating symptoms with hydration, fever reducers, and sometimes, bronchodilators or oxygen therapy for severe cases.

Prevention: 

Good hygiene practices like hand washing, avoiding close contact with sick people, and covering coughs and sneezes.

nodes.author: vikramwagh
nodes.text:
Diagnosis
Lab Testing: 
PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) from nasal or throat swabs is the most common method for detection.
Viral culture and serological tests are also used but less frequently.

nodes.author: vikramwagh
nodes.text:
Transmission: 
Spreads through respiratory droplets from coughing or sneezing, close personal contact, or touching surfaces contaminated with the virus.

Epidemiology
Seasonality: Typically peaks in winter and early spring in temperate climates, similar to other respiratory viruses.
Prevalence: Common worldwide, with infection rates similar to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).

nodes.author: vikramwagh
nodes.text:
Clinical Features
Symptoms: 
Respiratory symptoms similar to the common cold or flu, including cough, fever, nasal congestion, and shortness of breath.
In severe cases, especially in young children, the elderly, or immunocompromised individuals, it can cause bronchiolitis or pneumonia.
